description: BlueROV whisker dome as wired on 2026-10-29. Position = side L/R (port/starboard, the ROV's own left/right; L = +x) + F/B (front = the column nearer the dome's pole, back = the column at the widest part) + U/M/L (upper/middle/lower on the ROV). daq: the gauge channel and polarity of each bend axis, drag (front-back) and lift (up-down); default wiring drag = W<n>_A, lift = W<n>_B. Format: whisker_link/dome_map.py.
frame: collar frame of whiskers.json: mm, +z forward (tube axis), +y up, +x port
coordinates: PLACEHOLDER: root / axis copied from the CAD holes (rov-cad, whiskers.json), not measured on the built dome. 'asset side' in the notes is the CAD asset's own L/R label, which is the opposite (its L = -x = starboard); the assignment here follows the ROV frame
polarity_note: ASSUMPTION, confirm on the bench: identical sensors, each mounted with its drag gauge reading + when the tip bends toward the front, and its lift gauge + direction 90 deg counter-clockwise from the drag gauge's seen from the whisker tip looking at the dome (i.e. along axis x front). Then a positive lift reading means the tip goes DOWN on the port side and UP on starboard (axis x front flips with the side), so the port (L) lift gauges get polarity -1 and lift + = up on both sides. If the lift gauge is clockwise from drag instead, it is the starboard side that must flip. The overall sign of drag (does A + mean the tip bends forward?) is not known and is left at +1 everywhere.
